lines: וְטוּבְךָ לֹא יָמוּט כִּי הַכֹּל טוֹב
בַּמָּוֶת אוֹ בַּחַיִּים הִנֵּה הַכֹּל טוֹב

review: Each stanza is five lines whose first, second and fifth end on the same clause (فَالْكُلُّ خَيْر); Hebrew repeats כִּי הַכֹּל טוֹב at the same three points, because that refrain is the whole argument of the hymn.

1:3–1:4 אַתָּה בַּצָּר מְנוֹס / וּבָא מִמְּךָ חִלּוּץ — 'in distress You are the refuge, and from You comes rescue'; the Arabic الْمَنَاص is 'escape/refuge', and מָנוֹס is the biblical noun (Jer 25:35).

2:3–2:4 בְרִית אֱמֶת / כָל־הַמַּתָּנוֹת — the Arabic عَهْدُ ثَبَات and كُلُّ الْهِبَات are covenant and gifts; Hebrew uses בְּרִית with אֱמֶת (Neh 9:38) and the plural מַתָּנוֹת, which is post-biblical but the only word for 'gifts'.
2:5 בַּמָּוֶת אוֹ בַּחַיִּים — Romans 14:8 (אִם־נִחְיֶה לָאָדוֹן נִחְיֶה); the Arabic فَبِمَوْتٍ أَوْ حَيَاة is that verse and the line is left long deliberately, as in the print.
